newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico opposition legislators allege Clinton "snub".
newsitem.headline: Mexico opposition legislators allege Clinton "snub".

text.p: Mexican opposition senators complained on Wednesday that President Bill Clinton was breaking with tradition by ignoring them on his visit here next week.
Clinton's final official agenda for his May 5-7 visit has not yet been made public, but unofficial indications suggest he will not address the Mexican congress or visit the senate.
"The absence of the senate from President Clinton's visit is lamentable," said Gabriel Jimenez Remus, senate leader of the opposition National Action Party (PAN).
Hector Sanchez, senate leader of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), said the Mexican congress would be weakened in the eyes of the people if Clinton did not address it.
It appeared, he said, that the local congress "has no decision-making power and Clinton prefers to negotiate everything with President (Ernesto) Zedillo".
U.S. officials have said that Clinton plans a meeting with the leaders of Mexico's opposition parties during his trip.
Alfredo Ling, another PAN senator, said that by not addressing the senate, Clinton would break with protocol. All heads of state who visit the country have appeared in the senate, he said.
"It's not just a courtesy act, but is because of the very great importance which the Senate of the Republic has in Mexico's foreign relations," he said.

Fernando Solana, a former Mexican foreign minister and current senator for the governing Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), said he saw no special problem in Clinton not addressing the senate. There was no set tradition that this had to happen, he added.
